title: Extensions and Targets
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/0/body: Retracement levels sit **inside** the swing (below 100%). An **Extension** is a level **beyond 100% of the swing**. The most common are **127.2%** and **161.8%**, and they're used as **price targets** once the swing high (or low) breaks.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/1/body: Using the same swing from A to B: **extension = A + (swing length × ratio)**. So 127.2% is where price goes **27.2% of the swing length** above the high, and 161.8% is **61.8% of the swing length** above the high.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/1/tip: 1.272 is roughly the square root of 1.618, which is why it's used alongside the golden ratio.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/2/prompt: EUR/USD swung up from 1.0800 to 1.0900. Where's the 127.2% extension?
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/2/explanat: The swing is 100 pips and 27.2% of it is 27.2 pips: 1.0900 + 0.00272 = 1.09272. 1.09618 is the 161.8% level.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/3/statemen: The 161.8% extension is closer to the swing high than the 127.2% extension.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/3/explanat: 127.2% is only 27.2% of the swing above the high, while 161.8% is 61.8% of the swing above it. So 161.8% is the farther target.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/4/prompt: Bitcoin swung up from 60,000 to 64,000 and the swing high has now broken. Mark the 161.8% extension target with the line.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/4/explanat: The swing is $4,000 long. 161.8% extension = 60,000 + 1.618 × 4,000 = 66,472. Price has already passed the 127.2% level (65,088).
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/5/body: In a **downtrend**, do the same math **downward**: **extension = high − (swing length × ratio)**. These levels sit below the swing low and act as sell targets.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/6/prompt: GBP/USD swung down from 1.2800 to 1.2600, then the low broke. Which level is the ? line (1.24764)?
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/6/explanat: The swing is 200 pips. 1.2600 − 1.24764 = 123.6 pips, which is 61.8% of the swing below the low. So this is the 161.8% extension (1.2800 − 0.03236).
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/7/pairs/0/: Shallow pullback; a sign of a strong trend
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/7/pairs/1/: Deep pullback; edge of the golden zone
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/8/prompt: Gold's swing ran from 2300 to 2400. Tap the candle that reached the 127.2% extension and reacted to it.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l1/steps/8/explanat: 127.2% means 2400 + 27.2 = 2427.2. This candle's upper wick reached that line and it closed lower. The 2461.8 line is the 161.8% level, which price hasn't reached yet.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/0/body: A common approach when buying from a retracement zone: **target 1** is the previous swing high, **target 2** is the **127.2%** extension, and **target 3** is **161.8%**. You can close **part of your position** at each target and hold the rest.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/1/title: Do the math first, then enter
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/1/body: Before you enter, work out the distance to your **stop loss** and to each **target**. If even the first target doesn't give a good risk-to-reward, the trade isn't worth the risk.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/2/prompt: BTC's swing ran from 60,000 to 70,000. You bought at 64,000 with a stop at 62,000, and target 1 is the swing high (70,000). What's the risk-to-reward to target 1?
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/3/prompt: You bought at 2355. Price passed target 1 (2400) and has now printed a shooting star at the 127.2% extension. What's the most sensible move?
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/3/options/: Close part of the position and move the stop to entry
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/3/explanat: Price reached a key target and printed a reversal candle, so a pullback is now more likely. Taking some profit and moving your stop to entry locks in gains, and if the trend continues, you still ride the rest of the move.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/4/body: When price reaches **target 1**, many traders take some profit and move their **stop loss to the entry point (breakeven)**. That way, if the market turns, the rest of the trade closes with almost no loss.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/4/tip: Write your targets down before you enter, not in the heat of the trade.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/5/prompt: Put the steps of a buy trade with Fib targets in order.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/5/items/0: Enter in the golden zone after a confirmation candle
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/5/items/1: Stop loss below 78.6% or the swing low
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/5/items/2: Close part of the position at the previous high
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/5/items/3: Move the stop loss to entry
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/5/explanat: The stop goes in together with the entry. After target 1, take partial profit and move to a breakeven stop. Finally, exit at the extensions.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/6/statemen: After the swing high breaks, price always continues to 161.8%, so it's best to close your whole position only there.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/6/explanat: No level is guaranteed; price may turn at the previous high or at 127.2%. Scaling out helps you lock in some profit earlier.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/7/sentence: If the distance from entry to your ___ is shorter than the distance from entry to your ___, your risk-to-reward is worse than 1:1.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l2/steps/7/explanat: Reward is the distance to the target and risk is the distance to the stop. If the target is closer than the stop, you're risking more to make less.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/0/body: A **projection (Trend-Based Fib Extension)** needs three points: the swing start **A**, the swing high **B**, and the pullback low **C**. You project the length of swing AB from point **C**; for example, the 100% target is **C + (B − A)**.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/1/body: Common projection targets are **61.8%, 100% and 161.8%** of swing AB. **100%** means the new swing (CD) is exactly as long as the first; this symmetry is also called **AB=CD**.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/2/prompt: On BTC: A = 60,000, B = 70,000 and C = 65,000. Where's the 100% projection target?
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/2/explanat: AB = 10,000. Project it from C: 65,000 + 10,000 = 75,000. 72,720 is the 127.2% extension of swing AB itself, not a projection.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/3/sentence: In a projection, you take the length of swing ___ and project it from point ___.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/3/explanat: A projection assumes the next swing (from C) is a ratio of the first swing (AB); for example, 100% means the same size.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/4/prompt: Points A and B are marked. To draw the projection, tap point **C**.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/4/explanat: C is the pullback low that formed after high B (65,000, a 50% retracement). From here you project the length of AB: the 100% target is 75,000.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/5/body: An **extension** (lesson 1) uses only the two points A and B, while a **projection** carries the length of AB forward from **C**. It works the same way in a downtrend, just downward: **C − (A − B)**.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/6/prompt: On EUR/USD: A = 1.0900, B = 1.0800 and C = 1.0850. Price stopped at the ? line (1.0750). What level is this?
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/6/explanat: AB is 100 pips, and 1.0850 − 0.0100 = 1.0750. So swing CD came out exactly the same size as AB. The 127.2% extension would have been at 1.07728.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/7/prompt: On gold: A = 2300, B = 2400 and C = 2361.8 (a 38.2% retracement). Where's the 100% projection target?
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/7/explanat: 2361.8 + 100 = 2461.8. Interestingly, that's also exactly the 161.8% extension of swing AB (2300 + 161.8). When two tools point to the same number, that area matters more.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/8/statemen: A 100% projection means the new swing from point C travels exactly as far as swing AB.
lessons/fibonacci-u2-l3/steps/8/explanat: The 100% target is the AB=CD symmetry: CD is the same length as AB. Still, it's a common target, not a rule.
